title: ABOUT THE AUTHOR
text: ABOUT THE AUTHOR Born in Hartford, Connecticut, Charlotte Perkins Gilman (1860–1935) was an A merican novelist, short story writer, poet, editor, lecturer, commercial artist, and utopian feminist. Though her schooling was limited and erratic—leaving her largely self-taught—she amassed a breadth of knowledge, pursuing intellectual studies, artistic endeavors, and feminist advocacy. She would go on to become an organizer of social reform and a prominent lecturer noted for her unorthodox concepts of marriage, women’s suffrage, humanism, and patriarchal subjugation. Gilman was the author of several poetry collections, novels and novellas, and nearly two hundred short stories, including The Yellow Wallpaper , which was inspired by a severe bout of postpartum depression. In 1994, she was inducted into the National Women’s Hall of Fame.
